measurement_history.fact: ANA inventory: staff gauge readings start 1982-07-01 and continue. Operator SGB-CPRM.
ANA inventory: telemetry starts 2000-08-01. No automatic level recorder is listed.
Data check: several one-day jumps of 3 to 4 m in 1989-1992 (for example 990 cm on 1992-07-01 to 03, then 612 cm), in raw (level 1) and consistent (level 2) months. Kept as published.
SGB: recent readings can be revised after field visits that include re-leveling of the staff gauges.
Not found: number and hour of daily readings, gauge moves, gauge zero elevation, any publisher statement on early accuracy.

amazon-tabatinga.public_notes: This gauge starts in 1982, so it covers only about 44 years. Values after 2023 have not yet been reviewed by Brazil's water agency, and a few days in 1989 to 1992 show jumps that look like recording errors.

measurement_history.fact: ANA inventory: staff gauge readings start 1972-06-01 and continue. Operator SGB-CPRM. No recorder listed.
ANA inventory: telemetry starts 2001-06-01.
Data check: ANA flags 13% of days in the 1990s as estimated, the highest share of any decade at this gauge.
measurement_history.source: derived from ANA HidroSerieHistorica status codes, station 14100000

measurement_history.fact: Not found: number and hour of daily readings, gauge moves, gauge zero history, any publisher statement on early accuracy.

amazon-manacapuru.public_notes: This record starts in 1972. About one day in eight in the 1990s was estimated by Brazil's water agency rather than read, and values after 2023 are not yet reviewed.

measurement_history.fact: Rio Negro levels at the port of Manaus have been measured daily since September 1902.
ANA inventory lists the staff gauge series from 1902-09-01 to 2014-06-01; the ANA historic file used here has reviewed values to 2014-12-30.
ANA inventory: telemetry starts 2001-06-01, so it overlaps the staff gauge series.

Join: this file uses the reviewed staff gauge series through 2014-12-30 and telemetry daily means from 2015-01-01. On 2,274 days in 2005-2014 that have both, telemetry minus staff gauge has a median of 0 cm and yearly medians between -1.2 and 0 cm, so the two share the same gauge zero and the join is continuous.
measurement_history.source: derived from ANA HidroSerieHistorica and DadosHidrometeorologicos, station 14990000

measurement_history.fact: SGB: Manaus levels use a local, arbitrary reference tied to the port staff gauge; subtract 7.00 m from a reading to refer it to sea level.
Not found: who reads the port gauge and at what hour, any documented gauge move or zero change, a CPRM note giving 6.83 m instead of 7.00 m (could not be opened).

amazon-manaus.public_notes: Manaus has one of the longest river records in the tropics, read daily at the port since 1902. Since 2015 the values come from an automatic sensor and have not yet been reviewed; we checked ten years where both exist and they agree to within about a centimeter on a typical day.

measurement_history.fact: An earlier staff gauge on the port pier was read daily 1927-1947 and in mid-1948; it was never tied to a benchmark and was destroyed by the 1953 flood. That older series is not in this file and does not share the current zero (likely 77 cm higher).
The current staff gauge was installed on a new pier on 22 Feb 1968. Its zero is 8.144 m below CPRM benchmark RN4. Daily readings have no gaps except 1969, which is missing.

An automatic recorder was installed a few km upstream in 1982, tied to the port gauge (its readings need an 11 cm reduction, and its well runs dry at low water). Satellite telemetry was added in 1985.
ANA inventory: recorder 1982-01-01 to 2013-09-01, telemetry from 1997-05-01.
Not found: number and hour of daily readings.

amazon-obidos.public_notes: This record starts in 1968 and has no data for 1969. An older gauge from 1927 to 1948 used a different zero, so it is left out. Values after 2023 are not yet reviewed.

measurement_history.fact: Embrapa: 95 years of uninterrupted daily records 1900-1994. The gauge is at the Brazilian Navy's 6th Naval District, and readings are released daily by the Navy's western nautical signaling service.
Gauge zero altitude is 82.15 m (Embrapa, citing BRASIL 1974).
ANA inventory: recorder 1996-04-01 to 1998-11-01, telemetry from 1996-04-01. Operator SGB-CPRM.
Not found: hour of the daily reading, gauge moves or zero changes, upstream dams affecting this site, any publisher statement on early accuracy.

paraguay-ladario.public_notes: Brazil's Navy has read this gauge every day since 1900, and the record has almost no gaps. Values below zero are real low-water readings, not errors. Values after 2023 are not yet reviewed.

measurement_history.fact: INA metadata: Prefectura Naval Argentina staff gauge (not automatic); INA lists no gauge zero elevation.
Yacyreta dam, downstream of Posadas, held its reservoir at 76 m from 1994 to 2006.
The reservoir was raised to 78 m in April 2006 and step by step to its design level of 83 m, reached 12-13 Feb 2011.
INA: filling Yacyreta to 83 m caused a significant change in river behavior at Posadas.
Not found: early reading practice, gauge zero or zero changes, gauge moves, recorder or telemetry start, any accuracy statement.

parana-posadas.public_notes: Since 1994 Posadas sits in the reservoir of the Yacyreta dam, which was raised in steps until 2011. Levels since then mostly reflect how the dam is run, so they cannot be compared directly with the river before the dam.

measurement_history.fact: INA/UTN report: the Prefectura series in INA's database starts 01 Jan 1901, with 72 missing days to June 2024.
The gauge zero is given differently across documents (41.95 m IGN, 42.01 m IGN, 42.39 m MOP; INA's database labels 42.39 as IGN). INA calls it uncertain.
An automatic level recorder was installed in 2013 and another automatic station on 21 Jan 2019. The INA series used here is the Prefectura staff gauge.
Not found: early reading hours and readings per day, gauge move dates, any early accuracy statement.

parana-corrientes.public_notes: This daily record from Argentina's Coast Guard gauge starts in 1901 and has very few missing days. The agency publishes no review flags, so recent values may still be corrected.

measurement_history.fact: INA/UTN report: the Prefectura series for Parana starts 31 Dec 1902, with 543 missing days to June 2024.
Prefectura gauge zero is 9.432 m IGN (INA-IGN survey, 2018).
A second national-network gauge about 500 m away agrees closely day to day, apart from scattered single days up to 1.5 m off; after 2020 the two differ by less than 0.25 m.
Not found: early reading hours and readings per day, gauge moves, telemetry start, early accuracy statement.

parana-parana.public_notes: This daily record starts in 1902; the first decade has about one day in ten missing. The agency publishes no review flags, so recent values may still be corrected.

measurement_history.fact: INA/UTN report: the Rosario gauge has records from 1884.
INA metadata: Prefectura staff gauge (not automatic), zero at 2.923 m IGN.
Antico et al. (2020) rescued the early Rosario record, re-digitized it and corrected errors from a gradual sinking of the gauge. Whether INA's series includes that correction is not stated.
Not found: reading hours and readings per day, gauge moves, telemetry start, whether the INA series includes the sinking correction.

parana-rosario.public_notes: Rosario's record goes back to 1884, one of the longest in South America. Researchers found the gauge slowly sank in its early decades, and it is not clear whether this copy of the data was corrected for that, so the earliest years are less certain.

measurement_history.fact: News report citing Paraguay's hydrology office: Asuncion records go back to 1904; in September 2024 the level fell to -1.02 m, below the gauge zero.
Not found: gauge zero elevation, who read the gauge in early years and how often, gauge moves, recorder or telemetry start, any accuracy statement.

paraguay-asuncion.public_notes: Paraguay's weather service posts this record as a web table with no review flags and no published gauge zero. Values below zero are real low-water readings.

measurement_history.fact: Data check: one value a day through 1975, mostly timestamped 09:00 (08:00 in 1898-1907 and 1969-73), which fits a once-daily manual staff reading; BoM does not say so.
Data check: several readings a day begin in 1976, which fits a continuous recorder; not stated by BoM.
Nearly all values carry BoM quality code E, 'unknown'. BoM maps NSW 'daily or spot data' to E. Codes A and B first appear in 1990-91.
Hume Dam, 16 km upstream of Albury, was built 1919-1936 and enlarged 1950-1961. Since then river levels at Albury mostly reflect dam releases.
Dartmouth Dam, upstream of Hume, was built 1973-1979.
Not found: who read the gauge, gauge moves, gauge zero or datum changes, telemetry start.

murray-albury.public_notes: Albury's record starts in 1885, but Australia's weather bureau rates the quality of almost every value before 1990 as unknown. Hume Dam, finished in 1936 just upstream, controls the river here, so levels before and after the dam measure different things.

measurement_history.fact: Data check: record starts with several readings a day, which fits a continuous recorder.
Many values in 1975-79 carry quality C (estimate); 27% of days in the 1970s are estimated.
Torrumbarry Weir (Lock 26), the nearest Murray weir upstream, was finished in 1924.
Not found: gauge moves, datum or zero changes, telemetry start, publisher accuracy statement.

murray-swanhill.public_notes: This record starts in late 1974. About a quarter of the days in the late 1970s were estimated by the data owner rather than measured.

measurement_history.fact: Euston Weir (Lock 15) was finished in 1937; its full supply level is 47.6 m and parts of it are removed during floods.
Data check: record starts with several readings a day. Values are water surface elevations near the weir level (about 42 to 52 m), not a local gauge height.
BoM lists two station entries for 414203 about 2.7 km apart; not explained. This file uses the entry that holds the daily mean series (station_id 2877981).
Many values carry quality C (estimate); 32% of days in the 1970s are estimated.
Not found: whether the gauge is above or below the weir, the datum name, gauge move dates, telemetry start.

murray-euston.public_notes: Euston sits at a weir, so its level depends partly on how the weir is set. The numbers are heights above a sea-level reference, not above a local gauge, and about a third of days in the late 1970s were estimated.

measurement_history.fact: The series starts 1895-02-01 with daily 08:00 readings for that year, all quality B (compromised).
No values between 1895-12-31 and 1972-06-21.
Record resumes with several readings a day; quality E (unknown) until 1988.
The Bourke lock and weir, about 7 km from town, was built in 1897 and rebuilt as a concrete weir in 1941. Whether the town gauge sits in the weir pool is not stated.
Not found: why 1896-1972 is missing, gauge moves and datum history.

darling-bourke.public_notes: The usable record at Bourke starts in mid-1972; there is one year from 1895 and then nothing for 76 years. Quality is rated unknown until 1988.

measurement_history.fact: MRC 2005 data inventory: daily water level for Chiang Saen from 1960.
The station moved on 15 Dec 1993; later values need a 0.62 m correction to compare with earlier ones. Data check: this API series jumps about +0.45 m on 16 Dec 1993, so it appears not corrected.
Researchers report that the Chiang Saen data they got from MRC had not been corrected for the 1993 shift.
MRC fitted automatic equipment and telemetry at mainstream stations including Chiang Saen in 2001-2006. MRC near-real-time levels are the 7 a.m. reading.
Upstream Chinese dams changed the flow: Manwan reservoir filled in 1992, after which dry-season level swings grew; the largest effect came after Nuozhadu was finished in 2014.
MRC: gauge zero 357.1 m above mean sea level.
Not found: reading hours before 2005, datum name.

mekong-chiangsaen.public_notes: The gauge moved in December 1993 and the published numbers were not adjusted, so levels after 1993 read roughly half a meter higher than they would at the old site. Dams upstream in China have changed the river here since the 1990s.

measurement_history.fact: MRC sources disagree on the start: a 2008 flood report says records began in 1913; MRC's 2005 inventory and this API start in 1923. Levels are read at the Kilometre 4 gauge.
MRC 2005 inventory lists gaps in 1940-41, 1945-46 and 1953-59. The API has the same gaps, apart from single isolated days in 1940, 1945 and 1956.
JICA: Vientiane KM4 gauge zero 158.040 m above mean sea level, Ko Lak datum.
Not found: dates of gauge moves, reason for the 1940s-1950s gaps, early reading hours, telemetry start.

mekong-vientiane.public_notes: Vientiane's record starts in 1923 but is missing about 11 years in the 1940s and 1950s. The river commission has not reviewed and approved these values, and its data are not openly licensed.

measurement_history.fact: MRC 2005 inventory: daily water level for Pakse from 1960.
Pakse was among the stations given automatic equipment under MRC's 2001-2006 network project.
MRC note: data for 2022-01-11 to 2022-12-01 were replaced with backup manual records from the station.
MRC: gauge zero 86.5 m above mean sea level.
Not found: gauge moves, datum name, early reading practice, telemetry start.

mekong-pakse.public_notes: Pakse has a complete daily record since 1960. The river commission has not formally approved these values, and its data are not openly licensed.

measurement_history.fact: MRC's 2005 data inventory lists Kratie daily water level for 1934-39, 1941-56, 1958-74 and 1980-2002, so 1940, 1957 and 1975-79 were not in MRC's files then. The API now has full values for those years; they are marked estimated here.

Khmer Rouge years. Chua et al. (2022) filled gaps in MRC data from paper records at MRC and Cambodia's water ministry but say some years stayed undocumented. No source found says how 1975-79 was produced.
MRC: gauge zero -1.08 m relative to mean sea level.
MRC note: gaps on 2024-11-11 to 13 were filled from telemetry.
Not found: any statement of the method used for 1975-79, gauge moves, early reading practice, datum name.

mekong-kratie.public_notes: Kratie's record has no gaps, even through the Khmer Rouge years of 1975 to 1979, but those years were missing from the river commission's files in 2005 and were added later without explanation. We mark them, plus 1940 and 1957, as estimated.
